title: Give every billable day a row on the timesheet

blocks.text: A contractor bills from a generated timesheet, one row per day. Clients on a monthly contract get a row for each day of the month; clients who order a fixed engagement get a row for each weekday of it, and their purchase order prints the engagement as a first and a last day ("from 2027-10-01 to 2027-10-07"). Last month a client paid for one day less than the contractor worked, and nobody could say which.
`Timesheet` already knows which days are weekdays. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Timesheet.java`:

items: `days(month)`: every day of a calendar month, in order;
`weekdays(first, last)`: the weekdays of an engagement, from its first day to its last, in order.

blocks.text: About three lines in total. The tests use months and engagements in 2027 and 2028.

cases.says: a month's rows start on its first day and are in order, without duplicates, all inside the month
a period's weekdays start on its first day and leave out Saturday and Sunday
a month has a row for its last day, 29 February in a leap year included
a month shorter than 31 days has no row for a day of the next month
a period includes the last day printed on the order, and a one-day period has one row

origin.section: datesUntil Leaves Out Its End Date

concepts: datesUntil excludes its end date, so a period given by its first and last day needs last.plusDays(1), while a range that already ends on an exclusive date needs nothing added.
